notes: EBIT is approximated as Operating income from Netflix’s consolidated statements of operations (in thousands in the filing; converted to absolute USD by multiplying by 1,000). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))

D&A is modeled using depreciation and amortization of property, equipment and intangibles from the cash flow statement; capex is modeled using purchases of property and equipment (cash flow line; converted to absolute USD). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))

NWC definition (for consistency across years) is: NWC = Other current assets − (Current content liabilities + Accounts payable + Accrued expenses and other liabilities + Deferred revenue). Cash, short-term investments, and short-term debt are excluded from operating working capital. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))
Tax rate uses Netflix FY2025 effective tax rate (0.14). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))

NOL balance is approximated as (state NOL carryforwards 1,018m + foreign NOL carryforwards 190m) disclosed in the income tax note; NOL utilization set to 0.80 per model input. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))
Current price uses the latest available quote at research time (2026-03-21).

Comps EV/NTM fields use EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA shown by StockAnalysis (current/trailing proxy). Exact EV/NTM multiples may differ if forward EV/EBITDA and forward revenue estimates are used. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dis/statistics/))

catalysts: Regulatory outcome and closing progress for the Warner Bros. integration plans discussed by management. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

Sustained ad revenue acceleration and continued margin expansion versus internal operating targets. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

Evidence that price/mix actions translate into resilient paid growth while limiting content cost creep (margin durability). ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))
company_overview: Netflix is a global streaming service monetized via paid memberships, with an increasing contribution from advertising. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

FY2025 revenue was $45,183,036,000 with operating income (EBIT proxy) of $13,326,603,000, implying a 0.295 operating margin. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))

Netflix’s 2026 operating plan emphasizes margin expansion alongside a continued ramp of its ads business. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))
current_context: In its January 20, 2026 shareholder letter, Netflix forecast 2026 revenue of $50.7B-$51.7B (+12%-14% YoY) and targeted an operating margin of 31.5%. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

Management highlighted a projected rough doubling of ad revenue in 2026 versus 2025 and reiterated a focus on improving the core content slate and product experience. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

The company reported Q4 2025 revenue growth of 18% YoY (+17% FX-neutral) and crossed 325M paid memberships during the quarter. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case top-line growth chains from the 2026 management range (+0.13 in 2026) and decelerates gradually through 2030 (0.12→0.09) to reflect a maturing base. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

Base-case EBIT margin expands from ~0.295 (2025 realized) toward a long-run ~0.30 target, consistent with management’s 31.5% operating margin target for 2026 and subsequent conservative mean reversion. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

Depreciation and capex are modeled as modest, declining/stable percentages of sales (D&A ~0.0073→0.0069; capex ~0.0140→0.0120) reflecting scale plus content lifecycle effects. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))

Working capital is modeled as persistently negative (NWC_pct_sales ~-0.133), reflecting Netflix’s cash conversion profile driven largely by accrued/content and deferred-revenue dynamics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Ad market volatility and slower-than-expected monetization could pressure the margin trajectory. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

Higher content costs, weaker engagement/retention, or competitive pricing could prevent EBIT margin from reaching the modeled 0.30 terminal run-rate. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))

Integration/regulatory delays (deal timing/antitrust) could raise uncertainty around reinvestment and expense run-rate. ([s22.q4cdn.com](https://s22.q4cdn.com/959853165/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/FINAL-Q4-25-Shareholder-Letter.pdf))

presentation.subtitle: Netflix (NFLX) DCF Input Package — Ad Growth + Operating Margin Expansion
valuation_summary: The DCF uses EBIT margin assumptions grounded in the company’s reported 2025 operating margin and its 2026 operating margin target. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm))
Terminal value is implemented via a Gordon-growth approach (terminal_growth 0.03) with WACC 0.09, consistent with a long-run, mature-media platform risk profile.

Peer triangulation uses EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA from selected streaming/media comps and forwards P/E where available (with EV multiples treated as a proxy for near-term). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dis/statistics/))
